title: Pronoun - Types, Cases, and Usage Rules

questions.question: Which case should be used after prepositions, 'let', 'except', and 'like'?
questions.rationale: Objective Case (me, him, her, us, them) is used after prepositions, 'let', 'except', and 'like', e.g., 'There is no disagreement between you and me.'

questions.question: What is the key difference between a Possessive Adjective and a Possessive Pronoun?
options: They are identical in every way
A Possessive Adjective requires a noun after it (my pen); a Possessive Pronoun does not (mine)
Possessive Pronouns are only used in questions
Possessive Adjectives are only used with plural nouns
questions.rationale: Possessive Adjectives require a noun after them ('my pen'), whereas Possessive Pronouns stand alone ('mine').

questions.question: "It is ___ who am involved in solving this." Choose the correct pronoun.
questions.rationale: Subjective Case is used after 'It is' and in comparisons — 'I' is correct here, not the objective 'me'.

questions.question: What is the Reflexive Pronoun form of 'They'?
questions.rationale: According to the pronoun case chart, the Reflexive Pronoun for 'They' is 'Themselves'.

questions.question: Which combination do indefinite singular pronouns like 'Somebody', 'Nobody', and 'Everyone' take?
questions.rationale: Indefinite singular pronouns such as Somebody, Nobody, No one, Someone, Everyone, Everybody take a Singular Verb plus the Possessive 'his', e.g., 'No one has completed his work.'

questions.question: "Either of the students ___ come." Choose the correct verb.
questions.rationale: In the 'Either of / Neither of / One of / Each of + Plural Noun' construction, a Singular Verb follows — so 'Either of the students has come' is correct.

questions.question: "One should always make the most of ___ time." Choose the correct option.
questions.rationale: When 'One' is used as a subject, its possessive form must be 'one's', not 'his/her' — 'One should always make the most of one's time' is correct.

questions.question: "They are wiser than ___." Choose the correct pronoun.
questions.rationale: Subjective Case is used after comparisons with 'than' and 'as' — 'They are wiser than he' is correct.

questions.question: What is the Possessive Adjective for 'We'?
questions.rationale: Per the pronoun case chart, the Possessive Adjective for 'We' is 'Our' (used before a noun, as in 'our pen'), while 'Ours' is the Possessive Pronoun.

questions.question: "Neither of the girls ___ doing her work." Choose the correct verb.
questions.rationale: 'Neither of + Plural Noun' takes a Singular Verb — 'Neither of the girls is doing her work' follows Rule 4.
